reason: E2 directly supports the first four premises by demonstrating that cryo-rolling and annealing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 produces a hierarchical microstructure with simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement. However, the fifth premise regarding high-temperature and corrosion stability is not supported by the cited evidence, as neither E1 nor E2 addresses these properties.
premises: Cryogenic rolling of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA generates high dislocation density and heterogeneous strain across phases
Subsequent controlled annealing promotes partial recrystallization and grain refinement while preserving lamellar architecture
The resulting hierarchical microstructure increases dislocation barrier density, raising yield and ultimate strengths
Preserved lamellar interfaces maintain sufficient work hardening for ductility
The refined structure stabilizes performance under high-temperature fluctuations and corrosive environments
